miningWatch.title: Mining Watch
miningWatch.subtitle: Tracking how mining is affecting Palawan's environment, communities, and Indigenous peoples.
miningWatch.disclaimer: This page is compiled from independent journalism and human-rights/environmental organizations for public awareness. It is not an official statement or position of the City Government of Puerto Princesa.
miningWatch.mapCaveat: Pins mark known mining sites at the barangay/municipality level, sourced from official MGB records and cited news reporting below — they are approximate locations, not surveyed concession boundaries. Tap a pin for details and sources.
miningWatch.forestLossHeading: Tree Cover Loss by Dominant Driver
miningWatch.forestLossSubtitle: What's actually clearing forest across Palawan province, 2001–2025, by dominant cause — from permanent conversion (agriculture, mining, settlements) to temporary disturbances (logging, fire) that can eventually regrow.
miningWatch.forestLossMiningNote: "Hard commodities" — mining and energy infrastructure — clears the least total area of any driver province-wide: about 1,257 hectares of roughly 224,000 lost since 2001, behind even permanent agriculture and shifting cultivation, which dominate by a wide margin. That number likely understates mining's real footprint: the 11 companies now operating in Palawan hold roughly 29,430 hectares in concessions, most not yet actively cleared, and mining roads open remote forest to logging and farming by others — clearing this chart attributes to those drivers instead, not to mining. Hectares aside, mining also targets old-growth primary forest and protected ancestral domains specifically (Mt. Mantalingahan, Bataraza, Brooke's Point — see the map above), and its damage reaches beyond the cleared footprint through water pollution, like the hexavalent chromium contamination documented near Rio Tuba below.
miningWatch.footerNote: Every article below links to its original, independently published source. If you spot an outdated or broken link, please open an issue on this project's GitHub repository.

transparency.disclaimerBody: Budget figures on this page are sourced directly from Puerto Princesa's official budget documents; infrastructure project figures are sourced from DPWH's public project database. Both are updated periodically, not in real time. Some figures (like the National Tax Allotment total) are derived from other stated figures where the source document doesn't state them outright — see the notes next to each figure for details.
